clue.text: A spread in the golf club, butane cooked

indicators.note: the cooked letters go in the middle of the club's name, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cooks with butane at the golf club and offers a spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the gas, and 'in' splits the club after its first letter; 'the golf club' reads as a place but is the club itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This nut paste is a popular sandwich spread.

clue.text: Softly standing on a 1p

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing upright means these words are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
1 is the Roman numeral I and p is a penny

explanation.surface: Something placed carefully on top of a penny coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns the whole run ONAIP upwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian marking meaning soft is written p, short for this word.

clue.text: Collected a service key to the front door

parts.note: Mass is the church service of the Eucharist
E is one of the musical keys

indicators.note: the front of the word door is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone gathers a service key that opens the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key to the front door' looks like one object; it is a key (E) and then the front of 'door', with 'to the' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather up, so amassed means gathered or collected.

clue.text: Not qualified until I'm trained by a journalist

indicators.note: something trained is shaped into a new form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist is training someone who stays unqualified until then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges UNTILIM into UNLIMIT, and 'by' sets ED beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified here means without limits or reservations, as in unqualified praise.

clue.text: See 1
Can turn into American groups

indicators.note: the turned word goes into the middle of the other piece, so one is placed inside

parts.note: US abbreviates the United States, so American

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading its letters backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tin can is turned into a group of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the container; 'turn' reads it backwards and 'into' places it within the American abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are sets or squads, such as military or police groups.

clue.text: Label hydrant placed inside a clump of trees

indicators.note: one letter is set within the other word, so this signals a container

parts.note: a ticket is a label or tag on goods
H is the abbreviation used on signs marking a fire hydrant

explanation.surface: A tagged fire hydrant is found inside a clump of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense group of bushes or small trees growing together is a copse or thicket.

clue.text: Sorry for dishing out gruel, fret!

indicators.note: serving food spreads it about, so these letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone apologises to a fussing cook who is serving porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishing out' rearranges GRUEL and FRET together.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling regret is feeling sorry or remorseful.

clue.text: Father in line to become qualified

indicators.note: the father goes in the middle of the line, so this is a container

parts.note: a cable is a line or wire
Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father queues up, hoping to become qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable is competent or able to do a job.

clue.text: Old sailors playing cards after six

indicators.note: the cards come after six, so they follow it in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
kings are court cards in a pack

explanation.surface: Old sailors gamble with cards after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: These Norse seafarers raided and traded by sea in the early Middle Ages.

clue.text: Smartened it up and fastened tank inside it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the short word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tank sits inside the fastened word, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: tied means fastened
a vat is a large tank for liquid

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up and secures a tank inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the first 'it' from the bottom in this down entry; 'inside' places the tank within the fastened word, and the final 'it' simply points back to that fastened thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to spruce up or make oneself look smart.

clue.text: Kim used one as he sorted out a joint problem

indicators.note: sorting things out puts them in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Kim made use of a remedy as he dealt with a sore joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges all fourteen letters of KIM USED ONE AS HE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the common name for prepatellar bursitis, a swelling at the knee caused by kneeling.

clue.text: See 11
Trainee policeman has bounder on film

parts.note: a cad is a bounder, a dishonourable man
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A trainee officer turns out to be a rogue in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the police or armed forces.

clue.text: Sick of drinking rubbish, you say, before Easter?

parts.note: crap is a vulgar word for rubbish

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, giving a single letter with the same sound

parts.note: the word is spoken and becomes the letter of matching sound
Lent is the season of fasting leading up to Easter

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with drinking junk in the run-up to Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' gives U, which sounds like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent describes the ill feeling that follows heavy drinking.

clue.text: Confident if you're holding catalogue?

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, so its letters run across them

explanation.surface: A confident person asks whether you have the catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans confIDENT IF Y'ou're; the question mark marks the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue items is to list and name them, a way of recognising each one.

clue.text: Way I'm acting could be puzzling

parts.note: E, east, is a direction or way

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The way I perform may leave people puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges IMACTING into NIGMATIC, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious and hard to understand is puzzling.

clue.text: Married in taxi I fuss about going back in Asia

indicators.note: the married letter is put in the taxi word, a container

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: going back means this part is read from right to left
the fuss goes round the I, so one sits within the other

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A newly married person makes a fuss in a taxi on the way back in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ADO to give AIDO, and 'going back' turns it into ODIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country of South-East Asia, one found in that continent.

clue.text: Total ban on religion around Los Angeles

indicators.note: the ban goes round Los Angeles, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Los Angeles faces a complete ban on religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue places CE below BALAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance in an account is the total sum left.

clue.text: Model fish a student needed

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
L is the learner plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A model fish needs a student to look after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or model to follow.

clue.text: Fumes when former bowler takes us in

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the hat takes in the small word, holding it inside

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former cricket bowler lets us in.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is a hat, not a cricketer; HAT takes in US to give HAUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaust is the waste gas or fumes from an engine.

clue.text: Captain's order from the FA made us all mad

indicators.note: mad means wild and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A club captain's instruction from the Football Association drives everyone crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges THE FA MADE US ALL; FA is the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain gives this command to go forward at top speed.

clue.text: See 20
Sign sick note for char

indicators.note: feeling sick means out of sorts, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone signs a sick note for the cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges SIGN into SING. A char is also British slang for a cleaner, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to scorch or burn lightly on the surface.

clue.text: Large marble pathway

definitions.meaning: a big playing marble, also called a taw
a narrow lane or passage between buildings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a big marble used as a shooter and a narrow back lane.

clue.text: Writer Ann includes one good interpretation

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as me

indicators.note: Ann includes the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A writer called Ann gives a good interpretation of one text.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning is the sense or interpretation of something.

clue.text: Bravely push inside arch

indicators.note: the push goes inside the arch word, a container

parts.note: arch as an adjective means sly or knowing
to tout is to push or promote

explanation.surface: Someone bravely pushes into an archway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like a noun, but it is the adjective meaning sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stoutly is doing it resolutely and with courage.

clue.text: Article sells less £2 papers

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: less means take away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: L stands for pound, so two pounds is LL

explanation.surface: An item sells for under two pounds, as do the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes LL (two pounds, from the Latin libra) from SELLS, leaving SES.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are dissertations or academic papers.

clue.text: Pen jazz fan's taken, being absent-minded

indicators.note: the pen has taken the jazz fan in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz fan's pen has been taken by a forgetful friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty means scatterbrained and forgetful.
